blocks.content: This closing topic names the actual goal underlying every strategy covered in this module, and the one piece of configuration that is genuinely non-negotiable for achieving it: readiness probes.
1. The Shared Goal Behind Every Strategy
blocks.text: 1. The Shared Goal Behind Every Strategy

blocks.content: Rolling update, Recreate (deliberately excepted), blue-green, and canary are not four unrelated ideas, three of them share the exact same underlying goal, updating an application without users ever experiencing an interruption.

blocks.alt: One shared goal, three genuinely different ways of pursuing it

blocks.content: This connects directly, and critically, to the Health Checks module, none of these strategies actually deliver zero downtime without a properly configured readiness probe, it is not an optional nicety, it is foundational to the whole promise.

blocks.alt: Not an optional nicety, genuinely foundational to zero downtime actually working

blocks.content: Without a readiness probe, Kubernetes has no way to know a new Pod is not actually ready to serve traffic yet, it can start receiving real requests the instant its process starts, before it has finished initializing, exactly the failure mode a readiness probe, covered in its own topic, exists to prevent.

blocks.alt: The exact failure mode a readiness probe exists specifically to prevent

readinessProbe:
  httpGet:
    path: /ready
    port: 8080
  initialDelaySeconds: 5
  periodSeconds: 5

blocks.content: Genuinely achieving zero downtime needs three things together: a real, accurate readiness probe, graceful shutdown handling (the application responding correctly to SIGTERM, covered back in the Docker Containers module's docker stop topic), and a rollout strategy actually suited to the change being made.

blocks.alt: Three pieces, all needed together, not any single one in isolation

blocks.content: 5. The Four Strategies, Compared One Last Time
blocks.text: 5. The Four Strategies, Compared One Last Time

blocks.content: Put plainly, by downtime characteristics: Recreate accepts real downtime deliberately, rolling update avoids it (given a correct readiness probe), and blue-green and canary both avoid it too, while additionally offering safer, more controlled rollback than a plain rolling update alone.

blocks.alt: The complete picture, one final time, judged specifically by downtime and rollback safety

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: Zero downtime is the shared goal behind rolling update, blue-green, and canary, and a correctly configured readiness probe is genuinely non-negotiable for actually achieving it.
Real zero-downtime deployment needs three things together: an accurate readiness probe, graceful shutdown handling, and a rollout strategy actually suited to the change.
